clue.text: Hobby may be seen as part of this pastime

definitions.text: Hobby may be seen as part of this pastime

parts.words: Hobby may be seen as part of this pastime
parts.note: a hobby is also a small falcon, so the leisure interest being described is one where spotting such a falcon is the whole point

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a favourite leisure interest might be one aspect of some wider pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hobby' reads as a leisure interest, which chimes with 'pastime'; it is really the falcon of that name, one of the sights for a person out spotting wild species.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotting and recording wild species of feathered creatures is a popular outdoor pastime.

clue.text: Kind relation set up restaurants

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the whole run of kind plus relation is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: kind means sort, as in 'that kind of thing'
a sib is a sibling, a close relation

explanation.surface: A friendly family member opens a chain of eateries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns SORT + SIB as a single run, giving the small eateries.
explanation.definitionFit: Small informal French-style eating places are the plural of a word for a modest restaurant.

clue.text: Broadcast serial with East- Ender, down-to-earth type

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered far and wide, so the letters of serial are spread into a new order
the ender of a word is its final letter, here the last letter of East

explanation.surface: A soap opera featuring a cockney character from a London series is praised as grounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East-Ender' suggests a resident of London's East End or the BBC soap EastEnders, but it means the end of 'East': T. 'Broadcast' rearranges SERIAL into REALIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical person who sees things as they are is a down-to-earth type, the opposite of a dreamer.

clue.text: Campaign to expose unorthodox women spellers

definitions.text: Campaign to expose unorthodox women spellers

parts.words: Campaign to expose unorthodox women spellers
parts.note: spellers here are casters of spells, so the campaign is a pursuit of women who practise magic, and by extension any persecution of dissenters

explanation.surface: Some kind of drive is mounted against women who spell words in eccentric ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spellers' suggests people who spell words; it means people who cast spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A persecution of supposed sorceresses, extended to any campaign against people with unpopular views.

clue.text: Unspeakable batsman upset over ducks

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means this piece sits above the next
in a down clue, upset means the word for the batsman is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a bat is a cricket batsman, as in 'a useful bat'
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so two ducks are two O's

explanation.surface: A cricketer, distraught at scoring nothing in two innings, cannot bring himself to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns BAT into TAB, placed 'over' OO in the down entry. A duck is a zero score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden is not to be mentioned, too unmentionable to say.

clue.text: Composer, with hesitation, used to carry weapon

parts.note: Gustav Holst, English composer of The Planets
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A composer, hesitating, was once in the habit of carrying a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to' looks like 'formerly', but it means 'employed to': the definition describes a gun case.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather case worn on a belt or under the arm, employed for carrying a pistol.

clue.text: New-look songwriter

parts.note: novel means new and original
lo is an old word for look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: A songwriter with a fresh image.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a Welsh songwriter and actor, writer of 'Keep the Home Fires Burning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was a famous Welsh composer of popular songs and musicals.

clue.text: President gets horse in area round Boston

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln, US president
a shire is a heavy English draught horse

explanation.surface: A president acquires a horse in the district surrounding a Massachusetts city.
explanation.walkthrough: Boston suggests Massachusetts, but there is an original Boston, a town in the English county of Lincolnshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The English Boston is a port town in this eastern county.

clue.text: Second type of coffee

explanation.surface: A moment's thought about a variety of brew.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a very brief moment; instant coffee is the soluble powdered kind.

clue.text: Nothing in the garden area could be so dear

indicators.note: in means the word for nothing is placed within the garden area

parts.note: a bed is a plot in a garden for flowers
love means nil, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: With nothing in the flowerbed, a garden could hardly be so cherished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing' is a zero score in tennis, and the flowerbed is the 'garden area'; 'could be so' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone much loved is dear to us; the two words are near synonyms.

clue.text: A long time, the age of stupidity?

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on a long era, calling it a time of folly.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cryptic: a donkey stands for a fool, so the years of donkeys would be an age of stupidity.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for a very long while; read literally, a donkey is a byword for a dim person.

clue.text: Old language is hard on the ears

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means these letters follow after the word for the ears

parts.note: corn grows in ears, so corn stands for the ears collectively
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An ancient tongue is said to sound harsh to the listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard on the ears' reads as unpleasant to hear, but 'the ears' are CORN (ears of corn). Cornish is the Celtic language of Cornwall, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Celtic tongue of Cornwall died out as a community language in the 18th century, so it is an old language.

clue.text: Flier coming in to Bognor to land

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the run of words Bognor to land

explanation.surface: A pilot is arriving at Bognor to touch down.
explanation.walkthrough: Bognor Regis is an English seaside town. 'Flier' suggests an aircraft or pilot; it is a small songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small European bunting, a bird and so a creature that flies.

clue.text: Composer's the final character in record

indicators.note: in means the final character is put inside the word for record

parts.note: to list is to record or note down
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A composer is the closing character in a gramophone disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' suggests a disc but means LIST; Z, the last letter of the alphabet, goes inside it. 'Composer's' is 'Composer is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and virtuoso pianist.

clue.text: Endured no changes? That's rare

indicators.note: changes means the letters of endured no are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who has put up with no variation in life is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges ENDURED NO. 'rare' suggests uncommon, but it is meat that is lightly cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked rare is lightly cooked, pink inside.

clue.text: Devious card-player from Mississippi etc.

parts.note: deep means cunning or devious, as in 'a deep one'
South is one of the four players in bridge

explanation.surface: A crafty gambler from the Mississippi region, among others.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: The southeastern US states, including Mississippi and Alabama, form a region known by this name.

clue.text: Law imprisons Parisian and Oscar, say

indicators.note: imprisons means the word for law surrounds the French word, holding it inside

parts.note: a statute is a written law
et is French for and, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Legislation locks up a Frenchman and Oscar Wilde, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests a person, perhaps Wilde; it is the Academy Award trophy. 'Parisian and' is the French word for and.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is a small gold figure awarded by the Academy, an example of a small sculpted figure.

clue.text: Senior officer a Royal Marine laid out

indicators.note: laid out suggests spread or arranged differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A high-ranking officer floors a marine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges A, RM and LAID; 'laid out' reads as knocked flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval officer of the highest rank, commanding a fleet.

clue.text: Honourable Conservative slogan

explanation.surface: A decent rallying cry for the Tories.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads as 'Up (with the) Right!', a cheer for the political right, which Conservatives represent.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright means honest and moral; 'Up Right!' would be a cheer for the political right wing.

clue.text: Weary expressions similar, we hear, to an extent

indicators.note: similar, we hear means the answer sounds like the word for an extent when said aloud

parts.note: size is extent or magnitude

explanation.surface: Tired remarks are alike to some degree, it is reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to an extent' reads as 'somewhat', but 'an extent' is SIZE, and the answer sounds like it.
explanation.definitionFit: Long audible breaths let out from weariness or sadness are expressions of tiredness.

clue.text: He can combine elements of a couple of painters

definitions.text: He can combine elements of a couple of painters

parts.words: He can combine elements of a couple of painters
parts.note: a painter is also a rope used to tie up a boat, and joining two ropes by interweaving their strands is the job described

explanation.surface: An artist who can blend features of two painters' styles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painters' suggests artists, but a painter is also a boat's mooring rope; ropes are joined by interweaving their strands.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who joins two ropes by interweaving their strands does just such combining.

clue.text: Silly people including a number of Italian citizens

indicators.note: including means the word for silly people holds the number inside it

parts.note: geese are silly people, from 'silly goose'
no is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Foolish folk, among them several Italians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number' suggests several; it is NO, the abbreviation, placed inside GEESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Genoa, the northern Italian port city.

clue.text: Living always with no end of lust?

definitions.text: Living always with no end of lust?

indicators.note: with no means the letter that follows is removed from the word for living always

parts.note: immortal means living for ever

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the word lust is taken

explanation.surface: A person who lives for ever, with endless lust, is morally lax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' takes the T ('end of lust') out of IMMORTAL. The whole clue also describes the answer: an everlasting life of unending lust would be wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless lust would be wicked, against moral standards.

clue.text: Deposit for a house

explanation.surface: A down payment for a home.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge is to deposit or place something; a lodge is a small house, such as a gatekeeper's cottage.

clue.text: Refusal to speak in gag

explanation.surface: Someone declines to talk while gagged.
explanation.definitionFit: Silence is the absence of speech; to gag someone is to stop them talking.

clue.text: Printers" measure gets newspaper editor angry

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of width, half an em
a rag is a disparaging term for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A typographic unit sends a newspaper editor into a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a unit of width in printing, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious and incensed, someone driven into a rage is very angry.

clue.text: Indistinct, relative to hard centre

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: centre means the middle letters of the word hard are taken

explanation.surface: Something blurry, compared with a solid core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relative to' reads as 'compared with', but 'relative' is UNCLE and 'to' just joins it to AR, the centre of 'hard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Indistinct means hard to make out, blurred and not clear.

clue.text: A creature of habit when it comes to drying

definitions.text: A creature of habit when it comes to drying

parts.words: A creature of habit when it comes to drying
parts.note: habit means clothing, so a creature of habit is a frame-shaped beast that carries garments while they dry

explanation.surface: Someone sticks to a fixed routine for drying their washing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creature of habit' reads as someone set in routine; 'habit' is dress and the 'creature' is a horse, the name of a frame for airing laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden frame on which laundry is hung to dry or air indoors.
